title: Troubleshoot Windows Autopilot enrollment: event IDs, profile registry, MDM diagnostics and auto-collected logs
problem: When Autopilot stalls in OOBE the error page rarely names the cause. Work the flow in order (profile, tenant match, Entra join, MDM enrollment, ESP/apps) and pull the evidence from the device and from Intune instead of guessing.
steps: Locate the failure in the flow: network > profile download > user auth > Entra join > automatic MDM enrollment > settings/apps (ESP for classic, tracked apps/scripts for device preparation). If you see the ESP on a device meant for device preparation, it's running classic Autopilot.
Device preparation: start at Devices > Monitor > Windows Autopilot device preparation deployments; the device detail shows the last phase and which app or script failed or was Skipped.

Classic Autopilot on Windows 11: enable the diagnostics page in the ESP profile (Show app and profile configuration progress = Yes, Turn on log collection and diagnostics page for end users = Yes) and open it in OOBE with Ctrl+Shift+D.

In OOBE, Shift+F10 gives a prompt. Read the Autopilot channel: `Get-WinEvent -LogName 'Microsoft-Windows-ModernDeployment-Diagnostics-Provider/Autopilot' -MaxEvents 50 | Format-Table TimeCreated,Id,Message -Wrap`. Key IDs: 807 ZtdDeviceIsNotRegistered, 809/815 no assigned profile, 908 serial or product key mismatch, 171/172 TPM attestation (self-deploying/pre-provisioning), 163 profile already present.

Check what the device actually received: `Get-ItemProperty HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Provisioning\Diagnostics\Autopilot`. CloudAssignedTenantDomain blank or IsAutopilotDisabled = 1 means no registration or no profile download; TenantMatched = 0 means the user signed in to a different tenant than the device is registered to.

MDM side: `Get-WinEvent -LogName 'Microsoft-Windows-DeviceManagement-Enterprise-Diagnostics-Provider/Admin' -MaxEvents 50`, plus `dsregcmd /status` for join state. Enable the Debug channel in Event Viewer when Admin isn't enough.

Bundle everything: `mdmdiagnosticstool.exe -area "DeviceEnrollment;DeviceProvisioning;Autopilot" -zip C:\Users\Public\Documents\MDMDiagReport.zip`. The zip holds Autopilot and provisioning ETLs, MDMDiagHtmlReport.html, a registry dump and the enterprise diagnostics evtx.

From the portal: Intune auto-captures logs on Autopilot failure (one set per device per day, kept 28 days) under the device > Diagnostics > Download; for enrolled corporate devices use Collect diagnostics (bulk up to 25). Graph can't collect or download these.
After a profile change, restart from OOBE with `shutdown.exe /r /t 0` so the device downloads the profile again.
pitfalls: A device that boots into OOBE before any profile exists can cache an empty profile. Create and assign the profile first, then restart the device.

Re-using a pre-provisioned or self-deploying device returns 0x80180014 until you select Unblock device on its Autopilot record. The same code appears when Windows (MDM) is blocked in a device platform restriction.

Known policy conflicts during device ESP: AppLocker CSP, DeviceLock password rules that break autologon after reboot, disabling the Microsoft Account Sign-in Assistant (wlidsvc), AutoAdminLogon = 0, and PreferredAadTenantDomainName. Target those to users or apply after enrollment.
Classic ESP can't install LOB (MSI) and Win32 apps at the same time ('Another installation is in progress'). Use one type, or device preparation, which supports both.
Deleting the Entra device object created at registration breaks Autopilot targeting and join. Recover by deleting and re-importing the Autopilot device, not by recreating the Entra object.
done_when: The failing phase is identified from the deployment report, Autopilot event IDs or the profile registry values.
An MDM diagnostics zip or the Intune auto-collected logs for the device are saved with the ticket.
The fix is applied and a rerun reaches the desktop (classic) or Success in the device preparation report.

troubleshooting.symptom: Event 807 or 815 in the Autopilot log.
troubleshooting.fix: Confirm the hash is registered and the device is in a group targeted by a deployment profile; Sync in Intune, then restart OOBE.

troubleshooting.symptom: Event 908 SerialNumberMismatch / ProductKeyIdMismatch, or Fix pending after a repair.
troubleshooting.fix: Hardware changed (e.g. motherboard). Deregister and re-register the device with a fresh hash.

troubleshooting.symptom: 'Can't connect to the URL of your organization's MDM terms of use'.
troubleshooting.fix: Give the user a valid Intune, EMS or Microsoft 365 license that includes Intune.

troubleshooting.symptom: Join type shows Microsoft Entra registered instead of joined.
troubleshooting.fix: The device was workplace joined before. Delete it from Intune and Autopilot in the documented order, re-register and redeploy.

troubleshooting.symptom: Error 80180018 on the Something went wrong page.
troubleshooting.fix: Check user licensing and the user's device limits: the Entra join limit (default 50) and any Intune device limit restriction.

rollback: Turn the Debug channel of DeviceManagement-Enterprise-Diagnostics-Provider back off and delete exported zips and CSVs from the device and your workstation; they contain device and user identifiers.

If you changed the ESP profile to show the diagnostics page for a pilot, set Turn on log collection and diagnostics page for end users back to No when the pilot ends, if you don't want users to see it.
If you unblocked a device or moved a device between profiles, verify the Autopilot record shows the intended profile and assignment status before handing it back.
